name: Islamic Manners
description: Good manners and character (adab and akhlaq)

questions.question: What should we say when we meet another Muslim?
questions.explanation: We greet with 'As-salamu alaykum' — peace be upon you — and it spreads love between us.

questions.question: Which hand should we eat with?
questions.explanation: The Prophet taught us to eat and drink with the right hand.

questions.question: What do we say before we start eating?
questions.explanation: We say Bismillah before eating so our meal is blessed.

questions.question: How should we treat our parents?
questions.explanation: Islam teaches us to be kind and respectful to our parents at all times.

questions.question: What did the Prophet say about smiling at others?
options: It is a waste of time
questions.explanation: The Prophet said that smiling at your brother is a form of charity (sadaqah).

questions.question: What should we do when someone is talking to us?
questions.explanation: Good manners means listening carefully and not interrupting others.

questions.question: Should a Muslim tell lies?
questions.explanation: A Muslim always tells the truth. The Prophet was called Al-Amin, the Trustworthy.

questions.question: What should we do with our food if we don't want to finish it?
questions.explanation: Islam teaches us never to waste food or water — wasting is disliked by Allah.

questions.question: How should we speak to our teachers?
questions.explanation: Respecting teachers is part of Islamic manners because they give us knowledge.

questions.question: What should we do when we make a promise?
questions.explanation: A Muslim keeps promises. Breaking promises is a sign of weak character.

questions.question: What should we do if we hurt someone's feelings?
options: Say sorry and make it right
questions.explanation: We apologize and ask forgiveness — from the person and from Allah.

questions.question: How should we treat animals?
questions.explanation: The Prophet taught mercy to animals — even giving water to a thirsty dog brings reward.

questions.question: The Prophet said cleanliness is what part of faith?
questions.explanation: The Prophet said 'Cleanliness is half of faith', so Muslims keep themselves and their places clean.

questions.question: What is 'gheebah' (backbiting)?
options: Talking badly about someone who is not there
questions.explanation: Gheebah is saying bad things about someone behind their back — a big sin in Islam.

questions.question: What should we do when we feel very angry?
options: Stay calm and seek refuge in Allah
questions.explanation: The Prophet taught us to control anger, say A'udhu billah, and even sit down or make wudu.

questions.question: What did the Prophet say about the strong person?
options: The one who lifts heavy things
The one who controls himself when angry
questions.explanation: The Prophet said the truly strong person is the one who controls himself when angry.

questions.question: What should we do when we visit someone's home?
options: Stay as long as we want
questions.explanation: Islam teaches us to seek permission and greet before entering someone's home.

questions.question: What is a good deed we can do when someone is sick?
options: Visit them and make dua for them
questions.explanation: Visiting the sick is a beloved deed in Islam and brings great reward.

questions.question: What should we cover when we yawn?
questions.explanation: The Prophet taught us to cover our mouth when yawning.

questions.question: How should we treat our neighbors?
options: Be kind and never harm them
questions.explanation: The Prophet said whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should honor his neighbor.

questions.question: What manners should we have at the dinner table?
options: Eat from what is closest to us
questions.explanation: The Prophet taught: say Bismillah, eat with the right hand, and eat from what is near you.

questions.question: What did the Prophet teach about complaining about food?
questions.explanation: The Prophet never criticized food — if he liked it he ate it, if not he simply left it.

questions.question: Who should we greet with salam?
options: Those we know and those we don't know
questions.explanation: The Prophet taught us to spread salam to everyone, known and unknown.

questions.question: What is 'sadaqah'?
questions.explanation: Sadaqah is any voluntary act of giving or kindness — even a smile counts.

questions.question: What does 'akhlaq' mean?
questions.explanation: Akhlaq means our character and behavior. The Prophet came to perfect good akhlaq.

questions.question: The Prophet said the best among you are those who are best to whom?
questions.explanation: The Prophet said: 'The best of you are those who are best to their families.'

questions.question: What will be the heaviest thing on the scale of deeds on the Day of Judgment?
questions.explanation: The Prophet said nothing is heavier on the scale than good character.

questions.question: What is 'birrul-walidayn'?
questions.explanation: Birrul-walidayn means being dutiful and kind to parents — one of the greatest deeds in Islam.

questions.question: In the Quran, Allah says do not even say what word to your parents?
questions.explanation: Allah teaches us not to say even 'uff' to our parents — no word of disrespect at all.

questions.question: What is the Islamic teaching about keeping secrets (amanah)?
options: A trust must be kept faithfully
questions.explanation: An amanah (trust) — like a secret or borrowed item — must be guarded faithfully.

questions.question: What did the Prophet say about a person who does not thank people?
questions.explanation: The Prophet said whoever does not thank people has not thanked Allah.

questions.question: What is 'husn adh-dhann'?
questions.explanation: Husn adh-dhann means having a good opinion of others instead of assuming the worst.

questions.question: What should we do before sleeping, according to the Sunnah?
options: Make wudu and say the sleeping duas
questions.explanation: The Sunnah includes making wudu, reciting protective surahs, and sleeping on the right side.

questions.question: Why should we lower our voice when speaking?
options: The Quran praises a gentle, humble voice
questions.explanation: In the Quran, Luqman advised his son to lower his voice — humility is beautiful.

questions.question: What is the reward for removing something harmful from the road?
options: It is a charity and brings reward
questions.explanation: The Prophet taught that removing harm from people's path is a branch of faith and a charity.

questions.question: The Prophet said: 'I was only sent to perfect...' what?
questions.explanation: The Prophet said he was sent to perfect noble character (makarim al-akhlaq).
